$comment: Draft from the search-intel design page of 2026-10-30 (competitor ads on search result pages). One row per ad, not per competitor: intel/1's competitors list has no room for ad text, first and last sighting or a count.
title: intel.ads/1
description: The ads competitors (and the client) were seen running on search result pages: the words as published, where and when they were seen and how often. search-intel writes it from repeated samples of the pages; the makers and operators of paid search read it.
x-consumers: the maker of ad copy and the paid search operators
x-rules: The words are as published: never rewritten, translated or completed; a description the platform cut short stays cut and says so (description_truncated).
An ad is one advertiser and one headline start; the wordings the platform assembled for it on different searches are its variants, and the newest is the one shown.
The rows are a sample of searches, never a census: an ad not seen is not an ad not run, and times_seen counts searches that showed it, not impressions.
Every row has a source and the days it was first and last seen; an absent optional key means unknown, never null and never an empty string.

producer.description: The pack that wrote the document (its CLI word).

produced_at.description: When the document was written: ISO 8601 with its zone.

ads.description: The ads seen; empty when none was looked for.

market.description: The market the search was made in (the hub's market word).

language.description: The language of the words, an ISO 639-1 code.

advertiser.description: The advertiser's display name as the ad showed it.

display_url.description: The URL the ad displayed, as shown.

headline.description: The headline text as published, its parts in one string.

description_truncated.description: True when the platform cut the description short.

sitelinks.description: The titles of the ad's sitelinks.

keywords.description: The searches it was seen on.

first_seen.description: The day it was first seen, YYYY-MM-DD.

last_seen.description: The day it was last seen, YYYY-MM-DD.

variants.description: How many different wordings it was seen with.

role.description: What the owner decided the advertiser is.

source.description: Where the page was read (the tool or dataset).
